summary: Tanzania Immigration's visa guidelines say a visa can be obtained online through its official website, which they recommend, or on arrival at an official entry point; the ordinary visa costs 50 USD, and US passport holders must apply for the multiple visa, which costs 100 USD. They say nationals of EAC member states, of SADC member countries except Comoro and of Commonwealth countries except the United Kingdom, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand are not required to apply for a visa. The UK Foreign Office says all visitors to mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, except residents, must have mandatory inbound travel insurance.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: WHO lists Tanzania as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries at risk of yellow fever transmission, including travellers who transited more than 12 hours through the airport of such a country.

source.name: WHO — Countries with risk of yellow fever transmission and countries requiring yellow fever vaccination

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: The Government of Canada says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas and/or during a certain time of year in Tanzania, that antimalarial medication may be recommended depending on your itinerary and the time of year, that you should consult a health care professional, ideally 6 weeks before travel, and that you should protect yourself from mosquito bites at all times.

source.name: Government of Canada — Tanzania travel advice (health)

travelInsurance.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors to mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, except residents, must have mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought only for the first port of entry: from the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) if they arrive in mainland Tanzania first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) if they arrive in Zanzibar first, for the duration of the stay up to 92 days, as other travel insurance policies are not accepted. It can be bought online or at ports of entry on arrival, and visitors without it may be refused entry.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tanzania entry requirements

Visitors without the required insurance may be refused entry.

declarations.name: Zanzibar mandatory travel insurance

fee.notes: Inclusive of all charges, per visitor; covers stays of up to 92 consecutive days.

declarations.submitWindow: buy online before arrival or at the point of entry to Zanzibar
declarations.text: The UK Foreign Office says visitors (except residents) who arrive in Zanzibar first must buy travel insurance from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation. The Corporation says proof of other international insurance coverage is not accepted, that the policy is valid inside Tanzania for a maximum of 92 consecutive days, and that only one policy per visitor is allowed per trip.

source.name: Zanzibar Insurance Corporation — Mandatory Inbound Travel Insurance, FAQs (Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar)

currencyLimits.text: The Government of Canada says you must declare all currencies exceeding 10,000 U.S. dollars upon arrival in and departure from Tanzania.

source.name: Government of Canada — Tanzania travel advice (money)

notes: The UK Foreign Office says plastic bags are banned: if you arrive by air you will be asked to hand over all plastic bags on arrival, although zip-lock bags for airline security procedures are not included.
Canada's travel advice says you must obtain a permit to import a drone into Tanzania, and points to the Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority for information.

The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to take wildlife items, including horns and seashells, out of Tanzania without a certified export permit from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism, and advises not to bring animal skin accessories into the country, as you risk questioning or detention when leaving.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office (FCDO) advises against all but essential travel to any area within 20km of Tanzania's border with the Cabo Delgado province of Mozambique, due to attacks by groups linked with Islamic extremism. It also says tourists in Dar es Salaam have been 'express kidnapped': assaulted, robbed and forced with the threat of violence to withdraw cash from ATMs, and that it is safest to arrange a taxi through a hotel or travel operator.

The UK Foreign Office says the length of rainy seasons can vary, but they generally run from the end of March to May and from October to mid-December; Canada says that on the mainland the rainy season usually extends from March to May and then again from November to December.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must have mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought only for the first port of entry, for the duration of the stay up to 92 days: from the National Insurance Corporation if you arrive on the mainland first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation if you arrive in Zanzibar first, as other travel insurance policies are not accepted. The Zanzibar Insurance Corporation says its policy costs US $44 per visitor.

Tanzania's visa guidelines say American nationals are not entitled to the ordinary visa (50 USD) and must apply for the multiple visa (100 USD), which may be issued for a maximum validity of twelve months.

Tanzania's visa guidelines say a visa can also be obtained on arrival at an official entry point, but recommend the online application, made only through the official Tanzania Immigration Services website and not through any other online links.

The UK Foreign Office says plastic bags are banned in Tanzania and that if you arrive by air you'll be asked to hand over all plastic bags; the ban does not include zip-lock bags for airline security procedures.
Uganda's Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control says the East African Tourist Visa allows the traveller to travel to Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda only.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tanzania?
faq.answer: Tanzania Immigration's visa guidelines say nationals of EAC member states, of SADC member countries except Comoro and of Commonwealth countries except the United Kingdom, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand are not required to apply for a visa. Other visitors coming for tourism must apply for the ordinary visa (50 USD), online or on arrival at an official entry point, except US passport holders, who must apply for the multiple visa (100 USD).

faq.question: Does the Tanzanian visa cover Zanzibar?
faq.answer: Yes. Tanzania's visa guidelines say a visitor to both Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar selects the first destination on the form and is allowed to visit both places without a new visa. The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must have mandatory inbound travel insurance and only need to buy it for their first port of entry: from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation if they arrive in Zanzibar first, or from the National Insurance Corporation if they arrive on the mainland first. The Zanzibar Insurance Corporation says its policy costs US $44 per visitor.

faq.question: Can I get a Tanzanian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Tanzania's visa guidelines list the countries whose nationals are eligible for both the online and the on-arrival visa. Nationals of the countries on their no-visa-on-arrival list (among them Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria) cannot obtain a visa on arrival unless they have special permission from the Commissioner General of Immigration, and stateless persons and refugees must obtain a visa in advance. The guidelines recommend the online application.

faq.question: Why do US citizens pay more for a Tanzanian visa?
faq.answer: Tanzania's visa guidelines say that, due to bilateral agreements between Tanzania and America, American nationals are not entitled to the ordinary visa, so US passport holders who wish to visit for tourism or holiday must apply for the multiple visa (100 USD) even if they plan a single entry. It may be issued for a maximum validity of twelve months.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Tanzania?
faq.answer: WHO lists Tanzania as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries at risk of yellow fever transmission, including travellers who transited more than 12 hours through the airport of such a country.

faq.question: Is the East Africa Tourist Visa valid for Tanzania?
faq.answer: No. Uganda's Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control says the East African Tourist Visa allows the traveller to travel to Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda only.

summary.text: There are two options available for obtaining Tanzania Visa. The first option is obtaining Visa by applying online through Tanzania Immigration Services official website (www.immigration.go.tz) ; and the second option is obtaining Visa on arrival at official entry point. It is recommended to use online Visa application platform.
The fee for Ordinary Visa is 50 USD and has a validity of up to 90 days;
All visitors wishing to come for tourism purposes are required to apply for an Ordinary Visa EXCEPT American nationals (USA Passport holders) who are required to apply for Multiple Visa;
The fee for Multiple Visa is 100 USD and has a validity of 1 year.

There are several countries whose nationals are not required to apply for Visa to enter Tanzania. These are EAC Member State countries, SADC member countries except Comoro and Commonwealth countries except United Kingdom, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand.
All visitors to mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, except residents, must have mandatory inbound travel insurance.

faq.zanzibar-same-visa.text: If an applicant wishes to visit both Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar, he/she is advised to select his first destination while filling the form. But he will be allowed to visit both places without a need for a new Visa;
All visitors to mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, except residents, must have mandatory inbound travel insurance.
You only need to buy insurance for your first port of entry, either mainland Tanzania or Zanzibar.
If you arrive in Zanzibar first, you must: buy travel insurance from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) for the duration of your stay, up to 92 days
If you arrive in mainland Tanzania first, you must: buy travel insurance from the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) for the duration of your stay, up to 92 days
The cost of this policy is US $ 44 and is inclusive of all charges per visitor.

faq.visa-on-arrival.text: Nationals from the listed countries below are eligible for both Online as well as on arrival Visa facility.

Nationals from the list below cannot obtain Visa upon arrival unless they have obtained a special permission from Commissioner General of Immigration. These are: Afghanistan Bangladesh Burkina Faso Chad Eritrea Guinea Conakry Guinea Bissau Iran Iraq Kyrgyz Republic (Kyrgyzstan) Lebanon Mali Mauritania Niger Pakistan Palestine Somalia Syria
Also stateless persons or persons with refugee status cannot obtain visa upon arrival. They must apply and obtain visa in advance.
It is recommended to use online Visa application platform.

countryFacts.safety.text: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to any area within 20km of the Tanzanian border with the Cabo Delgado province of Mozambique, due to attacks by groups linked with Islamic extremism.
In Dar es Salaam, tourists have been ‘express kidnapped’. This means they’ve been assaulted, robbed and forced with the threat of violence to withdraw cash from ATMs.
It is safest to arrange a taxi through a hotel or travel operator.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The length of rainy seasons can vary, but they generally run from: the end of March to May October to mid-December
On the mainland, the rainy season usually extends from March to May and then again from November to December.
